Other tram cities like Munich or Berlin are flatter in their central districts; Dresden/Leipzig have broader boulevards and different stop signage styles.

There are single-span tram wires without visible rails (likely embedded), a bus/tram stop-style tall rectangular sign on the right sidewalk, and a blue parking or information sign mid-left. These specific alignments suggest a central Stuttgart feeder street descending toward a civic/office building. Exact street name cannot be confirmed from the visible details, but it resembles inner-district streets leading toward the city center within the basin.
Elimination summary: Non-continental cues (US/UK road markings, left-hand traffic) are absent. Alpine countries (Austria/Switzerland) often show different stop sign shapes and signage typography; the overall street furniture matches Germany more closely. Within Germany, the hilly background and tram wiring make Stuttgart a plausible fit versus flatter cities like Berlin, Hamburg, or Hannover.
